title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: W is a class of weak equivalences in (Cat), presumably a basic localizer ('localisateur fondamental') in the sense later fixed in Pursuing Stacks and Cisinski. Hot(W) = W^{-1}(Cat), with localisation functor γ. The previous page asks whether γ sends an arbitrary (possibly infinite) coproduct X = ∐_{j∈J} X_j to a coproduct in Hot(W). That is, whether Hom_Hot(X,Y) → ∏_j Hom_Hot(X_j,Y) is bijective. Grothendieck notes that without a calculus of fractions neither injectivity nor surjectivity is clear.

Surjectivity. Assume each class φ_j : X_j ⇢ Y can be represented by a genuine functor f_j : X_j → Y'_j, together with a weak equivalence Y → Y'_j. For finite J_0 ⊂ J, form the amalgamated sum Y'_{J_0} = ∐_Y Y'_j (j∈J_0), i.e. the pushout under Y. Then take Y' = colim_{J_0} Y'_{J_0}, a filtered colimit. If Y → Y' is in W, the composites X_j → Y'_j → Y' assemble into f : X → Y'. This gives a preimage of (φ_j), hence surjectivity ('Donc il y aura ... surjectivité!').

Injectivity. Given f, g : X → Y' with γ(f_j) = γ(g_j) for all j, is γ(f) = γ(g)? He first says 'Mais oui, par le même argument'. The marginal note ('bon raf!' or similar) and the end of the page suggest he then had second thoughts.

The Lemma isolates the technical step. Given any family of weak equivalences α_j : Y → Y'_j, there is a weak equivalence α : Y → Y' and functors β_j : Y'_j → Y' with β_j α_j = α. Moreover, if the α_j are open or closed immersions (cosieves or sieves), Y' can be taken to be the gluing (recollement / amalgamated sum) of the Y'_j.

The marginal diagram gives the proof. Factor each α_j as Y → Ȳ'_j (a mapping-cylinder-type replacement, an immersion) followed by a retraction r_j : Ȳ'_j → Y'_j with section s_j, r_j s_j = id. One then glues the Ȳ'_j along Y and sets β_j = (inclusion)∘s_j. The point is the familiar 'cofibration + pushout' argument, with sieves and cosieves playing the role of cofibrations.

The page then reduces the whole question to this. Given f, g : ∐ X_j → Y with γ(f_j) = γ(g_j) for all j, show γ(f) = γ(g). He warns that f_j ~ g_j for all j does not imply f ~ g. The reason is that the homotopy relation is generated by elementary homotopies (natural transformations), and the length of the zig-zag needed for each j can be unbounded in j. One therefore needs a 'Kan'-type hypothesis on Y, or rather on some weakly equivalent Y' (Y → Y' in W), where homotopy is computed by a single step.

The next page turns to the analogous question for finite products (Corollaire 2). There the strategy is via A^∧ for a strict test category A, and the needed input is stability of W under finite products.
errors: Surjectivity assumes that every morphism X_j ⇢ Y in Hot(W) is represented by a functor X_j → Y'_j with Y → Y'_j in W, i.e. a one-sided fraction. In a bare localisation morphisms are zig-zags; this representation needs a fibrant ('Kan') replacement or calculus of fractions, which is exactly what is in doubt. This is a gap in the argument as written.

The step 'Y → Y'_J ∈ W' needs two things: stability of W under pushouts along suitable cofibration-like maps (sieves/cosieves or Dwyer-type maps), and stability under filtered colimits. Neither is stated or justified on this page. In (Cat), pushouts along arbitrary functors do not preserve weak equivalences, hence the immersion hypothesis.

In the marginal mapping-cylinder construction, β_j α_j = α holds only up to a natural transformation (s_j α_j ≠ ᾱ_j strictly), not on the nose as the Lemma states, unless the construction is arranged more carefully. This is harmless in Hot(W) but inaccurate as stated.

The initial 'Mais oui, par le même argument' for injectivity is retracted later on the page. The infinite coproduct case genuinely needs control of homotopy-chain length, i.e. a Kan-type replacement, as he notes.

ideas.what: Coproducts in the localised category W^{-1}(Cat) and whether the localisation functor preserves (infinite) coproducts
ideas.modern_name: Hot_W has small coproducts, preserved by localisation (localizers as homotopy theories / model structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski (Les préfaisceaux comme modèles des types d'homotopie, Astérisque 308, 2006), building on Grothendieck's Pursuing Stacks
ideas.where_published: Related questions on Hot_W and finite products are discussed in Pursuing Stacks (1983); exact treatment of coproducts unsure

ideas.what: Lemma: a family of weak equivalences out of Y can be dominated by a single weak equivalence Y → Y', via mapping cylinders and gluing along sieves/cosieves
ideas.modern_name: Pushouts/filtered colimits of cofibrant weak equivalences (left properness, Dwyer maps in Thomason's model structure on Cat)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason (1980) for Dwyer maps; standard model-category technique (Quillen)
ideas.where_published: Similar mapping-cylinder/sieve arguments appear in Pursuing Stacks; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Observation that componentwise homotopy f_j ~ g_j does not imply f ~ g on an infinite coproduct, because zig-zag lengths are unbounded; hence the need for Kan-type (fibrant) targets
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy relation is a single-step equivalence relation only for fibrant targets

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page on a technical foundational point: preservation of coproducts by W^{-1}(Cat). It uses standard mapping-cylinder and gluing tricks and correctly flags the infinite-zig-zag subtlety. The questions were later settled by Cisinski's theory of basic localizers, and nothing here appears to go beyond that literature.
transcription_corrections: First line: likely 'Si on a J ... Y'_{J_0} = ∐_Y Y'_j (j∈J_0)', an amalgamated sum over Y (small 'Y' subscript next to ∐), not a plain coproduct.
Second line: 'Y'_J = lim→ Y'_{J_0}, on aura Y → Y' ∈ W'.

Margin diagram: Y →(ᾱ_j) Ȳ'_j with maps r_j : Ȳ'_j → Y'_j and s_j : Y'_j → Ȳ'_j. The identity is more plausibly r_j s_j = id_{Y'_j} (section of the retraction), together with α : Y → Y' and β_j : Y'_j → Y' ('comm.' marks).
Margin note at the left reads something like 'bon raf!' or 'à voir!' (uncertain), boxed by a double stroke.
Last lines: '(Mais attention, ... que f_j ~ g_j ∀ j∈J n'implique pas f ~ g !) Il faudra une condition ... des hypothèses "Kan" sur Y, ou plutôt sur un Y' tel que (Y → Y') ∈ W'.
